name: Payment Request API
plain: Opens the browser's native pay sheet with saved cards and addresses.
meaning: The site sees only what the person approves: card or wallet token, shipping, email and phone if requested.

web.api: new PaymentRequest(methodData, details, options).show(), canMakePayment(), hasEnrolledInstrument()

access.prompt_ui: Browser payment sheet listing cards, addresses and wallets
access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Opens the browser's native pay sheet with saved cards and addresses.

fields.name: shippingAddress
fields.range: country, region, city, postalCode, recipient, phone

limits.headline: Can open the browser's pay sheet with saved cards and addresses you pick
limits.user_action: You tap Pay or a wallet button at checkout.
can: Show a pay sheet with your saved cards, wallets and addresses
Ask for your name, email, phone and shipping address
Send the store the details you approve
cannot: See all your saved cards at once
Pay without you tapping Pay in the sheet
Work the same in every browser; some show a limited sheet
Keep the details after the payment ends
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge, Safari and Samsung Internet show it. Firefox shows only a partial version.

story.what_it_is: The browser shows its own pay sheet with your saved cards and address.

marketing.name: Payment Request API
marketing.pitch: MDN says the API gives a consistent checkout flow, with the browser handling the payment sheet.

story.for_you: A pay sheet pops up from the browser with your saved cards and address. You pick, confirm and you are done without retyping.
story.for_makers: Makers get faster checkouts and fewer typing errors. The browser holds the card, so the shop can lean on it for trusted wallets like Google Pay and Apple Pay.

use_cases.example: A store opens the browser pay sheet and finishes your order in one step.
A takeout site fills your address and card from the browser.
A booking site reads your name and email from the sheet.
A game store buys coins with a saved card.
A shop only sees a token and not the full card number.
A news site sells an annual pass in one tap.

technical_bounds: Must be called from a user gesture
Merchant never sees the full card number from Chrome autofill without CVC

history.change: Payment Request ships on Chrome Android
basic-card deprecated; Google Pay and other handlers remain
